briossisampylat-joshua-weissman.reasoning: Directional review for one of nine buns as published, no burger fillings. Exact source weighs 30 g wheat flour with milk and water for a heated tangzhong, then 480 g additional wheat flour, milk, yeast, sugar, salt, eggs/yolk and butter. Two rises; 190 C for 16–20 min; listed egg wash and melted butter included, no sesame. Verified available carbohydrate 49.46 g per bun, of which the two wheat flour additions supply about 41.93 g; sugar about 5.88 g. Englyst et al. 2003 primary Table 1 (p. 331), French bakery brioche 101 g test portion, GI 70 (SEM 18), and Pasquier pain au lait 94 g, GI 63 (SEM 10), for whole comparators on the glucose scale. Kim et al. 2019 (doi:10.1017/S0007114518003446, Tables 1 and 2) commercial soft wheat roll, GI 56.2 (SEM 11.1), offers a structurally similar leaner comparator. Applying each separate point to 49.46 g gives comparison-only GK 34.62, 31.16, 27.80. Different tangzhong, ingredients, baking and moisture conditions prevent transfer of a point; no comparator is a measured match or a biological bound. The source-specific comparison and 49.46 g in the defined bare bun support a likely high load, not numeric approval. Do not assign whole bun GI to flour or add the same sugar twice. Re-review on ingredient, coating, cooking or size changes. Numeric GK remains withheld in the historic research-of-record.

hampurilaissampylat-moomie.reasoning: Directional review for one of nine buns as published, no burger fillings. Exact recipe: 473 g semi-coarse wheat flour, 223 g water, 32 g dough butter, 55 g shell-free egg, 56 g sugar, 8 g salt and 10 g dry yeast, two rises, 190 C for 15–18 min, with 48 g butter before and after bake and 9 g sesame topping included. The retained calculation scope incorrectly mentions an egg wash, but rows and recipe agree that the weighed 55 g egg goes in dough and only butter/sesame go on top; no second egg is modeled. Available carbohydrate 45.33 g per bun includes ~38.89 g from refined wheat flour and ~6.22 g sugar. Best independent comparisons: Scazzina et al. 2016 commercial Pagnottelle soft wheat flour roll with sugar (mean GI 62, also reported by study author slide no.22), Kim et al. 2019 (doi:10.1017/S0007114518003446, Tables 1 and 2) soft roll with wheat flour, sugar, milk/fat and yeast (GI 56.2), Wolever et al. 1994 Toronto hamburger bun (mean bread-scale GI 87, glucose-scale ~62 per 2021 supplementary table no. 2212; differing participants and protocol; no double-counting tables as separate studies). The food comparisons translate to comparison-only GK around 28.1 and 25.5. Choice of flour, absence of commercial milk formulation, sugar, butter finish and sesame limit equivalence. Scazzina studied a deliberately high-fibre low-GI sliced bread (41) that would cross the boundary here, but this bun does not replace wheat flour with a fibre-enriched material. No guarantee or lower bound is inferred. No final baked match or numeric approval. Re-review size, recipe, fat finish, sides or process changes.

rationale.fi: Arvio koskee yhtä ohjeen sämpylää, jossa on voita ja seesaminsiemeniä pinnalla. Se perustuu annoksen hiilihydraatteihin ja samantyyppisten vaaleiden sämpylöiden mittauksiin. Hampurilaisen täytteet eivät sisälly arvioon.

kevyet-briossisampylat-clever-carrot.reasoning: Directional review for one of nine buns as published, no burger fillings. Exact source uses 405 g strong and 45 g semi-coarse wheat flour with water, milk, yeast, sugar, egg, salt and butter. Two rises; 205 C for 15–20 minutes, optional oven steam, listed egg wash included, no sesame or post-bake butter. Verified available carbohydrate 41.27 g per bun, ~37.0 g from flour, ~3.89 g from sugar. Englyst et al. 2003 primary Table 1 p. 331 pain au lait (GI 63) and bakery brioche (GI 70) support a comparison only; both tested products were richer in fat by available carbohydrate than this lighter recipe. Independent alternatives for a less enriched matrix: Scazzina et al. 2016 soft wheat flour roll with sugar GI 62, Kim et al. 2019 soft wheat roll GI 56.2; their comparison-only GK at this portion is 25.59 and 23.19 respectively. Differences in fat, strong flour, raises and optional steam prevent a point assignment. The 20 boundary would correspond to GI about 48.46; Scazzina's deliberately high-fibre sliced bread GI 41 is a real contrary food design, inapplicable to this recipe's conventional white flour and low fibre. Moderate load cannot be ruled out biologically; likely high is a qualitative judgement for the exact published bare bun. Do not present an interval from comparator points or SEM. Keep the numeric HOLD. Re-review flour, steam, size and serving scope changes.
